title: A minor page fault, start to finish

prereqs.why: The sequence is the mechanism, and the order is the only thing being asked about.

statement:
A process reads from a page that is mapped but not currently present in its page table. The page happens to be in the page cache already — another process read the same file a moment ago — so this is a **minor** fault and no disk is touched.

Put the seven steps in the order they actually happen, from the instruction that triggers it to the instruction completing.

items: The kernel finds the page already resident in the page cache, so no disk read is needed.
The CPU executes a load from a virtual address.
The kernel returns from the trap, and the CPU re-executes the same instruction, which now completes.
The MMU walks the page table and finds the entry for that address marked not-present.
The kernel writes a valid page-table entry pointing at that physical frame, with the right permissions.
The CPU traps into the kernel, recording the faulting address and enough state to restart the instruction.
The kernel looks up the address in the process's memory map and confirms it falls inside a mapped region.

hints: Two of the seven happen in hardware before the kernel has been given control at all. Find those first and the rest is one path.
The last step is not "the kernel returns the value". Nothing in the kernel knows what the load was loading — it fixes the mapping and lets the instruction run again.
